newsitem.title: USA: Continental Airlines stands by its ads.
newsitem.headline: Continental Airlines stands by its ads.

text.p: Continental Airlines on Tuesday stood by a recent advertising campaign that was characterized by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani as "disparaging of the City of New York."

The campaign, launched last week, features billboard signs and radio spots encouraging flyers to chose New Jersey's Newark International Airport instead of New York's JFK and LaGuardia Airports when traveling in and out of New York City.
"We remain very willing to sit down with the Mayor to hear his specific objections to the campaign," Continental said in a statement.
It continued, "Our ads do not in any way disparage New York and it seems to us the Mayor is attempting to censor ads promoting convenient service for New Yorkers."

Among other slogans, billboard signs bearing the ads read: "You know that young, good looking, wiz kid who wants your job? He flies out of Newark," and "Need to feel like a real New Yorker? Eat a bagel on your way to Newark."
The airline's response followed a letter released by Giuliani ealier in the day in which he urged Continental to pull the ads immediately.

"These ads only foster a false stereotype of New York," the mayor said in the letter. "Continental made a mistake when they thought that by attacking New York they would win business from New Yorkers."
In its response, Continental said that New Yorkers are responding well to its new advertising campaign.
Newark has served as Continental's hub since 1986 and is the departure point for about 350 Continental flights a day, compared with 14 Continental departures a day from LaGuardia.
